title: Rare and common genetic variants shape single-cell immune gene expression
title_zh: 稀有和常见遗传变异塑造单细胞免疫基因表达
abstract: Understanding the genetic basis of gene expression can shed light on the regulatory mechanisms underlying complex traits and diseases1,2. Single-cell-resolved measures of RNA levels and single-cell expression quantitative trait loci have revealed genetic regulation that drives cell states and types across diverse tissues3. Here we describe phase 1 of TenK10K, which leverages single-cell RNA sequencing data from more than 5 million cells across 28 immune cell types, along with matched whole-genome sequencing data from 1,925 individuals. This provides power to detect associations for rare and low-frequency genetic variants that have largely been uncharacterized in their impact on cell-specific gene expression. We map the effects of both common and rare variants in a cell-type-specific manner using a recent method that increases power by modelling single cells directly rather than aggregated ‘pseudobulk’ counts. We identify putative common regulatory variants for 83% of all 21,404 genes tested and cumulative rare-variant signals for 47% of those genes. We explore how genetic effects vary across cell types and states, develop a framework to determine the degree of single-cell expression quantitative trait loci cell-type specificity and show that about half of the effects are observed only in one or a few cell types. By integrating our results with functional annotations and disease information, we further characterize the likely molecular modes of action for many disease-variant associations. Finally, we explore the effects that genetic variants have on gene expression across continuous cell states, and effects that vary cell-state abundance directly. Phase 1 of TenK10K takes single-cell RNA sequencing and matched whole-genome sequencing data from 1,925 individuals, enabling detection of associations for common and rare genetic variants, the latter of which have been uncharacterized in their impact on cell-specific gene expression.
abstract_zh: 了解基因表达的遗传基础，可揭示复杂性状和疾病背后的调控机制1,2。单细胞分辨率的RNA水平测量和单细胞表达数量性状位点分析，揭示了驱动多种组织中细胞状态和细胞类型的遗传调控3。本文介绍了TenK10K项目的第1阶段，该阶段利用28种免疫细胞类型中超过500万个细胞的单细胞RNA测序数据，以及1925名个体的配对全基因组测序数据。这使我们能够检测稀有和低频遗传变异的关联，而这些变异在细胞特异性基因表达中的影响此前大多未被刻画。我们采用一种最近的方法，直接对单细胞进行建模而非采用汇总的“假批量”计数，以细胞类型特异性的方式绘制常见和稀有变异的影响，从而提高检测效能。我们在21404个检测基因中，鉴定出83%的常见调控变异候选位点和47%的基因的累积稀有变异信号。我们探讨遗传效应如何随细胞类型和状态而变化，开发了一种框架来确定单细胞表达数量性状位点的细胞类型特异性程度，并表明约一半的效应仅在一到少数几种细胞类型中出现。通过将我们的结果与功能注释和疾病信息相结合，我们进一步刻画了许多疾病-变异关联的可能分子作用方式。最后，我们探讨遗传变异对跨越连续细胞状态的基因表达的影响，以及直接影响细胞状态丰度的效应。TenK10K项目第1阶段利用1925名个体的单细胞RNA测序和配对全基因组测序数据，从而能够检测常见和稀有遗传变异的关联，而稀有变异在细胞特异性基因表达中的影响此前未被刻画。
